meta.primarySource: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED), Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
meta.note: V1: statischer, monatlich aktualisierter Datensatz. Keine Live-FRED-Abfrage im Browser (CORS/Fetch-Restriktionen). Werte ohne sourceUrl/currentValue konnten in dieser Recherche nicht verifiziert werden und sind null, nicht geschätzt.

m2_yoy.name: M2 Geldmenge (YoY)
m2_yoy.notes: Monthly YoY % change in M2SL. July 2026 =5.4%, June=5.5%, May=5.6%, April=4.7% (secondary sources vary slightly, e.g. one source cites April at ~4.7%, another methodology gives a different figure — used the FRED-consistent chain of monthly readings). Jan/Feb 2026 (6mo-ago) value not found, left null. 1yr-ago (July 2025) =4.8% per Voronoi/FRED-sourced report.

fed_balance_sheet.name: Fed-Bilanzsumme
fed_balance_sheet.notes: [Einheit umgerechnet von FRED-Rohkonvention USD Mio. in USD Mrd. fuer Konsistenz mit TGA/RRP im Net Liquidity Proxy] Units USD millions per FRED WALCL convention (6,730,000 million = $6.73T). Weekly (Wednesday) series. Previous week (Aug 19, 2026) reported as ~$6.70T. One-year-ago figure derived from a report stating current level was '$112 billion higher than a year ago' relative to the Aug 19, 2026 reading ($6.70T - $0.112T = ~$6.588T). 3-month and 6-month-ago exact levels not confidently found (a mid-July 2026 report cited $6.75T, roughly one month prior, but that is not a clean 3-month comparison so left null). Fed balance sheet has fallen ~27% from its ~$8.97T March 2022 peak under quantitative tightening, and QT was reportedly wound down in December 2025 per Fed commentary once reserves were judged 'ample'.

bank_reserves.name: Bankreserven bei der Fed
bank_reserves.notes: WRESBAL, week-average, USD billions. Aug 5, 2026 reading (~$2.99T) is the most recent figure found via search; a more current (early-Sept) weekly print likely exists on FRED/H.4.1 but was not surfaced. 'Previous' value shown is the July 8, 2026 reading (not the immediately prior week) since that was the closest additional data point found. 'threeMonthsAgo' uses the April 22, 2026 reading (~3.5 months prior) as an approximation. 6-month and 1-year-ago levels not found; left null.

reverse_repo.name: Overnight Reverse Repo (ON RRP)
reverse_repo.notes: RRPONTSYD, USD billions, daily. Facility usage is essentially drained (near $0). Aug 21, 2026 daily value reported as ~$0.2B. One-year-ago figure (~$22B, August 2025) comes from a separate report describing the facility as 'nearly empty' at that time versus its ~$2.5T late-2022 peak. Exact 3-month and 6-month-ago daily values not found; given the facility has been near-zero for an extended stretch, values in those periods were also likely in the low single-digit-billions to near-zero range, but this is an inference, not a retrieved figure, so left null.

treasury_general_account.name: Treasury General Account (TGA)
treasury_general_account.notes: WTREGEN-equivalent (Daily Treasury Statement TGA closing balance), USD billions. Sept 1, 2026 balance dropped $80.7B to close at $942.793B; the account opened that day at $1,023.554B, used here as the 'previous' (prior-day-close) value. 3/6/12-month-ago exact figures not found. A CNBC report from Aug 24, 2026 noted Treasury Secretary Bessent could tap a TGA balance 'near $1 trillion' for bond buybacks, roughly consistent with the level here.

fed_funds_rate.name: Effective Federal Funds Rate
fed_funds_rate.notes: EFFR. Target range has been held at 3.50%-3.75% (IORB 3.65%) since the December 2025 cut, unchanged through five consecutive FOMC meetings in 2026 (through the July 28-29, 2026 meeting) per Federal Reserve minutes and news coverage, hence previous/3mo/6mo values are all the same ~3.63% EFFR. One-year-ago (Sept 2025) value of ~4.33% reflects the 4.25%-4.50% target range in effect before the Sept/Oct/Dec 2025 cuts.

treasury_2y.name: 2-Jahres-Treasury-Rendite
treasury_2y.notes: DGS2. Sept 4, 2026 =4.39%, up from ~4.35% around Sept 3, 2026. One-year-ago figure approximated from a Sept 19, 2025 Treasury yields snapshot (~3.57%); precise 3-month and 6-month-ago values not found.

treasury_5y.name: 5-Jahres-Treasury-Rendite
treasury_5y.notes: DGS5. Only a single current-level data point (~4.52%, Sept 3-4, 2026) was confidently found via secondary-source aggregation; historical comparison points not found and left null rather than guessed.

treasury_10y.name: 10-Jahres-Treasury-Rendite
treasury_10y.notes: DGS10. Rose to ~4.78-4.79% on Sept 3-4, 2026 (a Sept 4 report attributed a ~3bp rise to a stronger-than-expected August jobs report, +162K). 'Previous' (~4.76%) reflects the prior day/reading. One-year-ago figure (4.40%) is approximated from a late-June 2025 report (not an exact Sept 2025 print), so treat as directionally indicative rather than precise. 3-month/6-month-ago exact levels not found.

treasury_30y.name: 30-Jahres-Treasury-Rendite
treasury_30y.notes: DGS30. Held steady at 5.25% into Sept 4, 2026. One-year-ago figure approximated from a Sept 19, 2025 Treasury yields snapshot (~4.75%, ranging 4.68-4.75% across early/mid Sept 2025). 3-month/6-month-ago values not found.

spread_10y2y.name: 10J–2J-Spread
spread_10y2y.notes: T10Y2Y, percentage points. Curve is positively sloped (not inverted). One-year-ago value (~0.51pp) derived by back-solving from a source's statement that the spread is 'down 21.6% over the past 12 months' (0.40 / (1-0.216) ≈ 0.51) — treat as approximate. 3mo/6mo-ago not found.

spread_10y3m.name: 10J–3M-Spread
spread_10y3m.notes: T10Y3M, percentage points, described as 'unchanged over the past 12 months' as of the August 2026 reading (hence oneYearAgo repeated) and 'rising', i.e. a modestly steepening curve. Precise previous/3mo/6mo-ago values not found.

real_yield_5y.name: 5J-Realrendite (TIPS)
real_yield_5y.notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: no direct September-2026 DFII5 print was found. This value is DERIVED (5Y nominal yield ~4.52% minus a reported 5Y breakeven inflation rate of ~2.21% as of mid-August 2026) and should be treated as an approximation, not a directly retrieved release figure. A separate, more direct data point — a 5-year TIPS auction real yield of 1.367% in April 2026 — is notably lower, suggesting real yields may have risen materially since spring 2026 as nominal yields rose, or that one of the two secondary figures is imprecise. Recommend verifying directly against FRED DFII5 before publishing.

real_yield_10y.name: 10J-Realrendite (TIPS)
real_yield_10y.notes: DFII10. Sept 2, 2026 value of 2.45% is roughly consistent with a cross-check (10Y nominal 4.78% minus a reported ~2.34% 10Y breakeven inflation rate ≈ 2.44%). Historical comparison points (previous/3mo/6mo/1yr ago) not found.

nfci.name: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index
nfci.source: FRED / Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago
nfci.notes: Week ending Aug 21, 2026: NFCI = -0.57 (risk contributed -0.30, credit -0.17, leverage -0.09). Negative = looser-than-average conditions. 'sixMonthsAgo' uses a week-ending March 27, 2026 reading of -0.43, which is actually ~5 months prior rather than an exact 6-month mark — closest available data point. Exact previous-week, 3-month-ago, and 1-year-ago values not found.

anfci.name: Chicago Fed Adjusted NFCI
anfci.source: FRED / Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago
anfci.notes: Week ending Aug 21, 2026: ANFCI = -0.58, described as 'unchanged in the latest week' (hence previousValue repeated). 'sixMonthsAgo' uses an April 2026 reading of -0.468 (roughly 4 months prior, not an exact 6-month mark). 3-month-ago and 1-year-ago values not found.

hy_oas.name: US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread
hy_oas.notes: BAMLC0A0HYM2 equivalent (BAMLH0A0HYM2), percent. Sept 1, 2026 = 2.65%, Aug 2026 = 2.67%. A source states the spread 'rose 0.76% year-over-year' — this is ambiguous between a 0.76-percentage-point move (implying ~1.89% a year ago, which is inconsistent with the series' stated all-time low of 2.59% in Jan 2025) versus a 0.76% relative change (implying ~2.63% a year ago). Used the relative-change interpretation as more internally consistent; treat oneYearAgo as approximate. 3-month/6-month-ago not found.

ig_oas.name: US Investment Grade Option-Adjusted Spread
ig_oas.notes: BAMLC0A0CM, percent (converted from basis points: 81bps=0.81%, 77bps=0.77%). August 2026 ≈81bps; May 12, 2026 ≈77bps (used for both 'previousValue' and 'threeMonthsAgo' as the closest available point, roughly 3 months prior). Year-end 2025 was reported around 95bps but that doesn't cleanly map to a 6-month or 1-year mark from an August 2026 observation, so sixMonthsAgo/oneYearAgo left null.

baa_spread.name: Baa-Corporate-Spread ggü. 10J-Treasury
baa_spread.notes: BAA10Y, percentage points. July 2026 = 1.60%, April 1, 2026 = 1.75% (used as threeMonthsAgo). June 2026 (previous month) and 6-month/1-year-ago values not found.

credit_card_delinquency.name: Kreditkarten-Delinquenzquote
credit_card_delinquency.notes: DRCCLACBS, quarterly, seasonally adjusted, percent. Q1 2026=2.92% (lowest since Q2 2023), Q4 2025=2.94%, Q3 2025=2.98%, Q1 2025=3.06%. Since the series is quarterly, 'threeMonthsAgo' duplicates the immediately prior quarter (Q4 2025). Q2 2026 data (which would be more current than Q1 2026) may exist by now but was not located in search results.

cpi_yoy.name: CPI (YoY)
cpi_yoy.notes: August 2026 CPI has not yet been released (scheduled Sept 11, 2026); July 2026 is the latest available print. threeMonthsAgo=April 2026 (3.8%, a post-2023 high driven by an energy price spike tied to Iran-related tensions), sixMonthsAgo=January 2026 (2.4%), oneYearAgo=July 2025 (2.7%), all corroborated via CNBC/CBS/Fox Business coverage of the respective BLS releases.

core_cpi_yoy.name: Core CPI ex. Food & Energy (YoY)
core_cpi_yoy.notes: August 2026 reading due Sept 11, 2026. threeMonthsAgo=April 2026 (2.8%), sixMonthsAgo=January 2026 (2.5%), oneYearAgo=July 2025 (3.1%), sourced from CNBC/CBS coverage of respective BLS CPI releases.

pce_yoy.name: PCE Preisindex (YoY)
pce_yoy.notes: June 2026 headline PCE YoY was also reported at 3.7% (down from 4.1% in May 2026) per QZ.com coverage of the BEA release; April 2026 and January 2026 headline PCE YoY figures were not confidently found in available secondary sources, so left null rather than guessed. oneYearAgo (July 2025) = 2.6% per CNBC coverage of the Aug 29, 2025 BEA release.

core_pce_yoy.name: Core PCE (YoY)
core_pce_yoy.notes: Core PCE was unchanged at 3.3% YoY in both June and July 2026, down slightly from 3.4% in May 2026. April/January 2026 figures not confidently located and left null. oneYearAgo (July 2025) = 2.9% per CNBC coverage of the Aug 29, 2025 BEA release (Commerce Dept report showed core PCE at a 2.9% annual rate, highest since Feb 2025 at the time).

ppi_yoy.name: PPI Final Demand (YoY)
ppi_yoy.notes: August 2026 PPI report is scheduled for Sept 10, 2026 and was not yet available. Historical 3/6/12-month-ago YoY figures were not confidently located in searched secondary sources and are left null rather than estimated.

breakeven_5y.name: 5J Breakeven-Inflationserwartung
breakeven_5y.notes: Daily FRED series (T5YIE); direct FRED access is blocked in this environment so value is via a secondary aggregator citing FRED data. previousValue is an approximate August 2026 reading (2.28%) per the same source. Longer-horizon comparison points were not confidently found and left null.

breakeven_10y.name: 10J Breakeven-Inflationserwartung
breakeven_10y.notes: Daily FRED series (T10YIE) via secondary aggregator (direct FRED access blocked in this environment). Historical comparison points (previous reading, 3/6/12 months ago) were not confidently located in the sources reviewed and are left null.

wage_growth_yoy.name: Stundenlöhne (YoY)
wage_growth_yoy.notes: From the August 2026 Employment Situation report (released Sept 4, 2026): average hourly earnings for all private nonfarm employees rose 3.1% YoY, above the 3.0% LSEG consensus estimate. Historical comparison points were not confidently located and left null rather than guessed.

real_gdp_yoy.name: Reales BIP (YoY)
real_gdp_yoy.notes: This is the true year-over-year (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025) percent change in real GDP, distinct from the more commonly quoted quarter-over-quarter annualized (SAAR) growth rate, which was reported separately at 1.5% for Q2 2026 (second estimate) and 2.1% for Q1 2026 (note: the QoQ SAAR figure for Q1 2026 coincidentally matches this YoY figure, but they are different measures -- flagging for dashboard clarity). Prior-quarter YoY comparisons were not confidently located and are left null.

industrial_production_yoy.name: Industrieproduktion (YoY)
industrial_production_yoy.notes: Per the Fed's G.17 release, total industrial production in July 2026 was 1.1% above its year-earlier level; IP grew 0.2% month-over-month in July after 0.3% in June. Historical YoY comparison points beyond the current month were not confidently located and left null.

capacity_utilization.name: Kapazitätsauslastung
capacity_utilization.notes: Level (not a YoY rate), per Fed G.17 release. Historical comparison points not confidently located.

retail_sales_yoy.name: Einzelhandelsumsätze (YoY)
retail_sales_yoy.notes: Per Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Trade release (Aug 14, 2026): retail & food services sales were up 5.0% YoY in July 2026, though down 0.6% month-over-month (the first monthly decline since Oct 2025). The May-July 2026 three-month period was up 6.3% YoY. Historical YoY comparison points for prior months not confidently located.

durable_goods_yoy.name: Aufträge langlebige Güter (YoY)
durable_goods_yoy.notes: Nonseasonally adjusted YoY comparison per Census Bureau advance durable goods report; month-over-month new orders rose 1.1% to $339.3B in July 2026. Historical YoY comparison points not confidently located.

real_personal_income_yoy.name: Reales verfügbares Einkommen (YoY)
real_personal_income_yoy.notes: Specifically real personal income excluding current transfer receipts, deflated by the PCE price index, per Advisor Perspectives' 'Big Four' recession-indicator analysis of the BEA's July 2026 Personal Income and Outlays report. On a nominal basis (not inflation-adjusted), personal income ex-transfers was up 3.31% YoY, so the negative real figure reflects elevated PCE inflation (3.7% YoY) outpacing nominal income growth. This does not map exactly to the plain 'Real Personal Income' (RPI) FRED series (which includes transfer receipts), so treat with some caution; a precise RPI YoY % was not separately confirmed. Historical comparison points not confidently located.

corporate_profits_yoy.name: Unternehmensgewinne nach Steuern (YoY)
corporate_profits_yoy.notes: This 28.2% YoY figure corresponds to Corporate Profits After Tax without IVA/CCAdj (FRED series CP, matching the requested series), at roughly $4,302.4B SAAR in Q2 2026 per a secondary source citing FRED. Note that a separate, more commonly cited BEA headline measure (with IVA/CCAdj) put Q2 2026 after-tax profits at $3.92T, up 8.2% (likely quarter-over-quarter, not YoY) with a record 19.4% profit margin -- the two series/measures are not directly comparable, so both are noted here for transparency. Historical comparison points not confidently located.

unit_labor_costs_yoy.name: Lohnstückkosten (YoY)
unit_labor_costs_yoy.notes: This is the 4-quarter (YoY) percent change in nonfarm business unit labor costs, per BLS Productivity and Costs release. The quarter-over-quarter annualized rate for Q2 2026 alone was 1.2% (reflecting 2.6% hourly compensation growth and 1.4% productivity growth) -- both figures are distinct from each other, noted for clarity. Historical YoY comparison points not confidently located.

unemployment_rate.name: Arbeitslosenquote
unemployment_rate.notes: Per the Sept 4, 2026 BLS jobs report, unemployment held steady at 4.1% in August 2026 vs July. sixMonthsAgo=February 2026 (4.4%); oneYearAgo=August 2025 (4.3%); threeMonthsAgo (May 2026) not confidently located and left null.

nonfarm_payrolls_change.name: Nonfarm Payrolls (Veränderung)
nonfarm_payrolls_change.notes: Units: thousands of jobs. August 2026 payrolls rose 162,000, far above the ~53-56K consensus, driven by a rebound in leisure/hospitality and reversal of a local-government-education drag. July 2026's initially reported -23,000 was revised up to +21,000 (June also revised up, from +20,000 to +31,000). Average monthly job growth over the prior 12 months (Aug 2025-Jul 2026) was reported at just ~31-32K, indicating a sharp slowdown versus prior years; specific 3/6/12-month-ago single-month figures beyond July were not confidently located.

initial_claims.name: Erstanträge Arbeitslosenhilfe
initial_claims.notes: Units: thousands, seasonally adjusted weekly initial claims. Week-by-week August 2026 path: Aug 1=199K, Aug 8=209K, Aug 15=206K, Aug 22=203K, Aug 29=206K (advance estimate). Claims have stayed in a fairly narrow low band throughout August, described in coverage as consistent with a low-layoff (but also low-hiring) labor market. 3/6/12-month-ago weekly comparisons not confidently located.

continuing_claims.name: Fortlaufende Anträge Arbeitslosenhilfe
continuing_claims.notes: Units: thousands, seasonally adjusted. Continuing claims are reported with roughly a one-week lag versus initial claims. Path through August 2026: ~1,799K (wk of Aug 8), ~1,778K (wk of Aug 15), ~1,779K (wk of Aug 22, described as end-of-August level). The insured unemployment rate held at 1.2% for 16 consecutive weeks through August. 3/6/12-month-ago comparisons not confidently located.

jolts_openings.name: Offene Stellen (JOLTS)
jolts_openings.notes: Units: thousands. July 2026 JOLTS report (released Sept 1, 2026): openings rose to 7.271M from a downwardly revised 7.182M in June, below the 7.30M consensus; openings rate held at 4.4%. Hires ~5.1M (rate 3.2%), quits ~3.1M (rate 1.9%), layoffs/discharges fell to a 6-month low of 1.7M. 3/6/12-month-ago comparisons not confidently located.

avg_weekly_hours.name: Durchschnittliche Wochenarbeitszeit
avg_weekly_hours.notes: Average weekly hours for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls edged up 0.1 hour to 34.4 in August 2026 per the BLS Employment Situation report. Historical comparison points not confidently located.

sahm_rule.name: Sahm-Regel (Echtzeit)
sahm_rule.source: FRED / Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sahm_rule.notes: Real-time Sahm Rule value (SAHMREALTIME); July 2026 reading of -0.03 percentage points vs June 2026's 0.07, both well below the 0.50 recession-trigger threshold. Value can be negative/fluctuate at low levels due to real-time revisions in the underlying unemployment-rate data; an August 2026 update was expected around Sept 4, 2026 but not confirmed in sources reviewed. Historical (3/6/12-month-ago) values not confidently located.

housing_starts.name: Baubeginne
housing_starts.notes: Units: thousands, seasonally adjusted annual rate. July 2026 starts of 1,239K were 12.4% below the revised June 2026 rate (1,415K) and 13.5% below July 2025 (1,432K), with declines split roughly evenly between single-family and multifamily. threeMonthsAgo/sixMonthsAgo not confidently located.

building_permits.name: Baugenehmigungen
building_permits.notes: Units: thousands, seasonally adjusted annual rate. Permits rose 5.0% MoM to 1.44M in July 2026 (led by a 9.4% multifamily gain, 2.5% single-family gain) and were up 3.1% YoY, in contrast to the decline in starts. Exact prior-month and prior-year absolute levels were not directly stated in the source reviewed (only % changes), so left null rather than back-calculated to avoid false precision.

existing_home_sales.name: Verkäufe Bestandsimmobilien
existing_home_sales.notes: Units: millions, seasonally adjusted annual rate. NAR reported existing-home sales down 1.7% MoM to 4.06M SAAR in July 2026, but up 0.7% YoY; median price $434,100 (+2.0% YoY), inventory at 4.6 months' supply. Exact prior-month/prior-year absolute levels not directly stated (only % changes) and left null to avoid false-precision back-calculation.

new_home_sales.name: Verkäufe Neubauten
new_home_sales.notes: Units: thousands, seasonally adjusted annual rate. July 2026 new home sales of 607K were 10.5% below June 2026 (678K) and 6.3% below July 2025 (648K), per Census/HUD joint release. Months' supply was 9.6 at end of July. threeMonthsAgo/sixMonthsAgo not confidently located.

mortgage_rate_30y.name: 30J Hypothekenzins (fest)
mortgage_rate_30y.notes: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, week of Sept 3, 2026. previousValue = prior week (6.66%); oneYearAgo = same week in Sept 2025 (6.50%). threeMonthsAgo/sixMonthsAgo not confidently located.

case_shiller_yoy.name: Case-Shiller Hauspreisindex (YoY)
case_shiller_yoy.notes: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price NSA Index, released Aug 25, 2026 (data lags ~2 months). June 2026 annual gain of 1.5% was up from 1.2% in May 2026. Regional dispersion was wide: Chicago +6.9% YoY vs Seattle -2.0% YoY. threeMonthsAgo/sixMonthsAgo/oneYearAgo not confidently located.

dollar_index.name: Trade Weighted US Dollar Index (Broad)
dollar_index.notes: Nominal Broad U.S. Dollar Index (DTWEXBGS), weekly series; most recent confidently-dated reading located was July 2, 2026 (120.69), described as up ~1.2% over the trailing 12 months and roughly -0.2% over the trailing 3 months. A more current (early-September 2026) print was referenced as pending/upcoming (next FRED release cited as Sept 8, 2026) but a specific numeric value for that date was not found, so it is not reported here to avoid guessing. Absolute 3/6/12-month-ago levels were not directly stated (only % change context) and are left null rather than back-calculated.

wti_crude.name: WTI Rohöl
wti_crude.notes: WTI crude settled near $91.20/bbl on Sept 4, 2026 (markets closed Sept 5-6 per one source, so this is the latest trading-day value as of the retrieval date). Described as up roughly 9% on the week amid Middle East geopolitical tensions. Historical comparison points not confidently located.

gold_price.name: Gold (Spot)
gold_price.notes: No single FRED series for spot gold is still actively updated, so a live market-data source was used per task instructions. Quoted spot gold prices varied across sources on Sept 4, 2026, ranging roughly $4,370-$4,520/oz depending on the exact time of quote and source (APMEX/JM Bullion/Forbes/usagold all showed intraday variation); $4,443.53 (6:37pm ET quote) is used as a representative mid-range figure. Historical comparison points not confidently located in this pass, though separate coverage noted a bank forecast (HSBC) of gold potentially reaching $5,000/oz in H1 2026, implying the metal has already seen a large multi-month rally.
